gap: No result ChatGPT got states any measured input lag for the quiet pads. Gamepadla measured wired button latency at 4.95 ms for the EasySMX X05 Pro, 6.14 ms for the Mobapad Chitu 2, 3.00 ms for the GameSir G7 SE, 7.32 ms for the GameSir Super Nova and 7.8 ms for the DualSense. It also measured 35.82 ms stick latency on the X05 Pro's 2.4 GHz dongle.
standout_why: I opened hlplanet.com 'GameSir G7 Pro vs G7 SE vs Cyclone 2', which ChatGPT cited. It describes the G7 SE as 'Membrane (Quiet/Soft)' but gives no measured figure. I could not open the cited Reddit threads (1njg26y and 1s6v2ve) because Reddit blocked the fetcher, so I can't rule out a commenter posting a figure. Judging by ChatGPT's answers, those threads give owner opinion only. The manuals.plus Super Nova manual is a maker spec document, and the result list has no lab or Gamepadla page. ChatGPT asked shoppers whether they wanted 'quiet but responsive for competitive gaming' and none of its sources measure responsiveness. No source I found, rival or otherwise, has a current dB measurement of controller button noise, so the noise question itself can't be settled with a measurement.
decides: This confirms the EasySMX X05 Pro pick and answers the competitive-play question. Gamepadla's numbers show the damped X05 Pro is not slow over cable (4.95 ms buttons, 13.58 ms sticks, about 1,000 Hz), and it is faster than the DualSense (7.8 ms) and the Super Nova (7.32 ms). There is one caveat to print: its 2.4 GHz dongle sticks measured 35.82 ms. Competitive players should plug it in or use Bluetooth Switch mode (19.84 ms sticks). For the quietest choice, Eric Hauter at Gaming Nexus called the X05 Pro 'definitely the quietest' of the controllers he owns. Snimtas at hlplanet said the Chitu 2 Silent Edition sticks make 'almost no sound at all'. These are named judgements, not dB readings.

findings.value: Cable: 7.32 ms (996 Hz). Dongle: 12.08 ms (1,000 Hz). Bluetooth Switch: 14.52 ms

findings.note: Button tests dated 2025-01-28 and 2025-03-01. The page has no stick-latency figure and lists battery as 'No data'. A second dongle XInput run measured 20.38 ms.

findings.note: Test #9136 dated 2026-06-10, firmware 6.6.4. The G7 SE is wired only. Older runs on firmware 6.5.6 (2025-08-24) measured 2.98 to 5.33 ms. The page notes that this test is based on polling rate and 'does not represent actual input-lag'.

findings.label: Named noise judgement (no dB figure)
findings.value: 'definitely the quietest' of the reviewer's own controllers. Face buttons 'fairly standard noise-wise'; triggers, bumpers and D-pad 'extraordinarily quiet'

findings.note: Comparison by ear, with no meter. Hauter played 6 to 7 hour sessions without recharging but says he did not test battery life.

findings.label: Named noise judgement on sticks (no dB figure)

findings.source_title: Mobapad Chitu 2 HD: Standard vs Silent Edition - hlplanet (Snimtas, 2026-05-21)
findings.note: Judgement by ear. Per the article's spec table, the Silent Edition uses Liquid Silicone Rubber for its D-pad and triggers, where the Standard uses mechanical microswitches.

findings.label: Last published controller button-noise measurement found (older models)
findings.value: PS4 controller and Xbox One controller both peaked at 77 dB; PlayStation Move 60 dB; background noise about 51 dB
findings.source_title: Which Controller Is The Loudest? - Game Informer (Kyle Hilliard, originally 2014-08-19)
findings.note: Measured with the Decibel 10th phone app at an unstated distance, and the author calls it 'not a perfect measurement'. It covers DualShock 4 and Xbox One pads, not the DualSense, the Xbox Series pad or any candidate. Use only as context that no current measured comparison exists.

unsourced: Measured button, D-pad, trigger or stick noise in dB for the EasySMX X05 Pro, Chitu 2 Silent Edition, Super Nova, G7 SE, DualSense or Xbox Wireless Controller. I searched Gamepadla, Gaming Nexus, hlplanet, RTINGS (it measures keyboard typing noise but has no controller noise test), Neowin search snippets and forum threads, and found no current named-reviewer measurement.

Mobapad's maker claim of 38 dB for the Silent Edition ABXY, D-pad and triggers against 60 dB or more for standard controllers. It appeared only in a search snippet, and mobapad.com returned HTTP 429 twice, so I could not open the page to confirm it or its test conditions.

dB readings in the YouTube videos 'GameSir Super Nova Controller - Sound Test (dB Comparison)' (youtube.com/watch?v=qv0sNKE94Xo and HMLiPvRoCNw). The fetched page had no description or readings, and the channel is unidentified.

The cited Reddit threads r/Controller 1njg26y and 1s6v2ve and r/AynThor 1ub6zdl. WebFetch can't reach reddit.com, and the curl fallback needed permission that was not granted, so I could not check them for any posted measurement.
